candidate_sentences.text: Eleving Group delivered record financial results in 2024.
Revenue increased nearly 15% to EUR 216.6 million from EUR 189.3 million in 2023, while net interest income rose 16.9% to EUR 162.2 million.
Adjusted EBITDA reached a record EUR 89.8 million, up more than 16% from EUR 77.5 million.
Profit before tax increased to EUR 37.7 million from EUR 28.5 million, and total net profit rose 21% to an all-time high of EUR 29.6 million.
Growth was supported by a 26.8% increase in loan issuance to EUR 368.6 million and a 16% expansion in the net loan and vehicle-rental portfolio to EUR 371.2 million.

verified_key_information_units.information: Key year-over-year improvements included a 29.3% capitalization ratio (vs 26.1% in 2023), 2.4 interest coverage ratio (vs 2.3), and reduced net leverage to 3.3x (from 3.7x).

verified_key_information_units.information: Major performance drivers were organic growth in Europe/Africa, successful integration of Sub-Saharan operations (tripling regional portfolio), digital transformation (doubled applications, new self-service platform), and enhanced risk management improving portfolio quality.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: CEO keynote; Management report operations section

candidate_sentences.text: The largest portfolio increases came from Romania, Uganda, Albania, and the Sub-Saharan markets acquired in 2023.
The Group reported that integration of those operations tripled the combined portfolio across its three main regional markets.

Digitalization also supported demand and efficiency: the new self-service platform was rolled out across established European vehicle-finance markets, while vehicle-loan applications increased 80.9% year on year and total applications nearly doubled.
Portfolio quality improved alongside expansion.
Non-performing loan rates declined from 7.5% to 6.1% in vehicle finance and from 4.5% to 4.3% in consumer finance.
The ratio of impairment expense to interest revenue fell by two percentage points despite the larger portfolio, which the Group linked to continued underwriting discipline and risk management.

verified_key_information_units.information: Business segments showed vehicle finance (67% of portfolio: 45% traditional, 20% flexible/subscription) and consumer finance (33%: Kredo, Tigo, etc.), with key growth in East Africa (e-motorcycles), Romania, Uganda, and Albania offsetting exits from Balkan/Belarus.

details.completeness_justification: K1, K2, K3, K4, and K5 are all PRESENT with supporting evidence across multiple sentences. K6 is MISSING as there is no mention of strategic priorities, product portfolio expansion (e.g., electric motorcycle financing), geographic expansion plans, or ESG strategy development. K7 is MISSING as there is no reference to post-reporting period events such as the March 2025 bond tap or expected tax refund. While the summary covers most core financial and operational highlights, the absence of forward-looking strategic priorities (K6) and recent liquidity events (K7) prevents a 'Yes' rating, resulting in a 'Generally yes' assessment.
details.coherence_justification: The candidate summary is internally coherent. All statements build logically upon each other without contradictions. Revenue, profit, and portfolio growth figures are consistently presented across sentences. The explanation of one-off VAT liability (S15) and its exclusion in an adjusted profit figure (S16) is clear and non-contradictory. Portfolio quality improvements (S11-S13) align with growth figures. Capitalization changes (S17-S18) are explained through IPO proceeds usage (S19). The rating upgrade (S20) follows from strengthened capitalization. No material logical gaps, contradictions, or organizational issues are present.
